name: Microsoft / Fluent
era: Contemporary design system · authored web adaptation
idea: Quiet material layers and a clear command bar distinguish navigation, content and actions.
origin: Fluent is Microsoft’s cross-platform design language. Fluent 2 describes Solid, Mica, Acrylic and Smoke with different roles. This light web adaptation uses opaque surfaces and a tinted sidebar; it does not implement native Mica.
tip: Map navigation, content and transient layers first. Then choose materials and an opaque fallback.

finder.signature: Command bar, quiet navigation and distinct content surfaces.

markers: Demo: 168px navigation column; content uses the remaining space.
Demo: Horizontal command bar above the project list.
Demo: 8px radius on the shared content surface.
Demo: 1px outlines instead of shadows between rows.
Demo: Blue selection rail in the navigation.
Demo: 32px heading, 16px project text and 14px metadata.
Demo: Opaque white reading surface on a neutral ground.
Demo: System font; no embedded Segoe UI file.

params.radius: Demo: 4px; see markers for component variations.
params.contrast: Dark text on opaque light surfaces; focus and states are separate roles.
params.density: Compact navigation, roomier content; desktop rows at least 64px.
params.motion: Immediate view changes; no animated transitions in this comparison.

strengths: Quiet material layers and a clear command bar distinguish navigation, content and actions.
A documented system supports consistent component decisions.
risks: Translucency everywhere obscures the distinct roles of Fluent materials.
These colors, sizes and radii describe this demo, not a full vendor token specification.
The web adaptation does not reproduce native window management, assistive technology integration or device input.
a11y: Test visible keyboard focus, screen-reader names, 200% text resizing and contrast in every state. Use system colors for native implementations and retain text labels for status. These editorial scores are not an accessibility certification.
longevity: Stable hierarchy and task structure outlast individual theme generations. Check current platform components when implementing.
verdict: Quiet material layers and a clear command bar distinguish navigation, content and actions. Map navigation, content and transient layers first. Then choose materials and an opaque fallback.

platforms.web: Authored HTML/CSS comparison; use semantic controls in a product.
platforms.mobile: On smartphones the fixed sidebar disappears. Content groups, small radii and blue action hierarchy remain; controls grow to touch size. Mica is not simulated.
platforms.desktop: The broad reference shows the system’s task hierarchy. Actual native applications also need platform navigation and input conventions.
